messages:
Eli (Recruiting): quick one 1: contractor offer converted to FTE starting 12/01. Hiring manager asked if unused contractor sick days (we tracked as unpaid leave) can be converted to company sick bank as carryover. any precedent?

Sam (People Ops): interesting edge case. contractors don't accrue our paid sick usually, so there's no formal balance to convert. that said i've seen exceptions if contractor had documented paid sick under contract. do we have the contractor agreement?

Eli (Recruiting): contract said 5 days "sick allowance" paid out monthly. attached office note but not in HRIS. manager flagged it was an approved benefit.

Carlos (Manager): yea we approved those 5 days as part of conversion. i'd like to grant equivalent 5 paid sick days to their FTE balance on start date so they don't lose it. ok to do that?

Nisha (HRBP): policy check 1: converting external benefits to internal bank requires manager approval + People Ops + legal sign-off. We need proof of payment or the contract clause. Also track as a one-time credit with note "contract-to-FTE carryover". Can't change accrual rate permanently.

Legal Bot: Flag: confirm there are no tax implications for retroactive pay. If those 5 days were paid by contractor employer, converting to paid sick for new payroll may require payroll to treat as taxable benefit. Recommend payroll consult. Link: https://redwood.example/legal/benefits-conversion

PeopleOps Bot: Reminder: exceptions must be documented in the employee file. Use exception type: BENEFIT_CONVERSION and include manager approval.

Sam (People Ops): Proposed workflow:
1) Upload scanned contract clause to employee document store.
2) Manager posts single-line approval in thread.
3) People Ops creates exception record, adds +5 sick hours to HRIS on first day.
4) Notify payroll for tax handling.
If everyone agrees I'll proceed.

Carlos (Manager): i approve conversion of 5 contracted sick days to company sick bank for Lee Tran on 12/01.

Sam (People Ops): thanks. i'll open exception EXC-2024-415 and queue payroll. Jasper (HRIS) can you run the update on 12/01? Example HRIS command we use:
```
hrcli grant --user lee.tran --type SICK --amount 5 --note "Contract-to-FTE carryover approved by manager; EXC-2024-415"
```

Jasper L.: noted. i'll schedule it for 12/01 and cc payroll.

Eli (Recruiting): another quick note 1: Lee's manager also asked about taking PTO during the performance calibration week (first week of Jan) since we're usually in a blackout for reviews. manager asked if we can allow single-day exceptions.

Nisha (HRBP): performance calibration blackout (1st week of Jan) is in the policy to ensure reviewers present. Exceptions allowed for pre-approved emergencies or business-critical coverage only. For planned PTO, manager swaps coverage or approves single-day exceptions if they can attend calibration remotely. Document as CAL_BLOCK exception.

Carlos (Manager): so we should ask Lee to avoid taking PTO that week if possible, but if they need one day can approve as long as they're present for their calibration slot.

Sam (People Ops): TL;DR: contractor sick carryover is allowed as a documented exception with contract evidence + manager sign-off + payroll review. Performance blackout stays in place; single-day exceptions okay if calibration presence is maintained. I'll file EXC-2024-415 and update the offer conversion checklist. Closing unless payroll flags anything.

PeopleOps Bot: Action items created: EXC-2024-415, Payroll ticket PL-9987. See: https://redwood.example/hr/exceptions/EXC-2024-415

Jasper L.: Done. Scheduled HRIS grant for 2024-12-01 and notified payroll.

Sam (People Ops): thanks all :white_check_mark:
